paper_metadata.title: Modulation of phase separation and high-temperature mechanical properties by L12 phase in AlCoCrFeMo0.05Ni2 high-entropy alloy

evidence.quote: The high-temperature strengthening mechanism of the L12 phase in AlCoCrFeMo0.05Ni2 high-entropy alloy (HEA) remains unclear. This study investigates the high-temperature mechanical response of the L12 phase in this HEA using atomistic simulations.
This study presents a novel computational investigation into the high-temperature strengthening mechanism of the L1 2 phase in the AlCoCrFeMo 0.05 Ni ₂ HEA.

Simulation results revealed a pronounced phase decomposition phenomenon in the OM structure during tensile deformation.
At a strain of 0.105, elongated, Al-rich precipitates aligned along the tensile direction began to emerge within the matrix.
As the strain increased to 0.11, these elongated precipitates coarsened via Ostwald ripening, eventually transforming into equiaxed precipitates.

This phenomenon suggests the activation of various dislocation recovery and plastic deformation mechanisms, such as stacking fault recovery induced by increased stacking fault energy, deformation twinning, dynamic recovery processes, and potentially stress-induced phase transformations or vacancy cluster nucleation.
In the OM, dislocations may more readily overcome lattice friction stresses, facilitating movement via glide or cross-slip.

The incorporation of Mo aimed to enhance solid solution strengthening. The resulting lattice distortion destabilized the crystal lattice, thereby promoting phase decomposition and the formation of L12 precipitates.
This observation underscores the decisive role of structural order in promoting phase decomposition.
